args.query: Council on Tall Buildings and Urban Habitat Burj Khalifa height 828 m

observations.content:
Summary: The Burj Khalifa's official height is 828 metres (2,717 feet) to the architectural top, which includes the central spire. The absolute tip, including a small communications needle, reaches 829.8 metres (2,722 feet). The highest public access point is At The Top SKY on floor 148, at 585.4 metres (1,921 feet). The building has 163 floors above ground, plus 2 basement levels, with 160 habitable floors. The spire adds 244 metres (800 feet) to the total height.

[1] Burj Khalifa Height, Floors, and Honest Stats: What 828 Meters Actually Means · TBC
    https://tallestbuildingscouncil.org/articles/burj-khalifa-honest-stats
    Burj Khalifa's official height is 828 metres (2,717 feet). This is the architectural top - the tip of the central spire. The highest floor you can reach by elevator is floor 148, At The Top SKY, at 585.4 metres (1,921 feet).

The gap between these two numbers - 242.6 metres - is composed of the building's central spire and mechanical structure. This represents a 29.3% Vanity Ratio: 29.3% of the 828-metre headline figure is non-occupiable structure. [...] ## Burj Khalifa observation deck height

Burj Khalifa has two observation levels:

At The Top (floors 124-125): 452m elevation. This is the standard public observation deck.

At The Top SKY (floor 148): 585.4m elevation. This is the highest public access point of any building in the world - the genuine world record that actually matters. [...] This near-tie at honest height is one of the most interesting data points in the entire Honest 100. Two buildings, 196m apart in architectural height, are essentially tied in real-world occupancy altitude. Shanghai Tower achieves its 583.5m of occupied height in 632m of total structure (7.7% Vanity Ratio). Burj Khalifa achieves 585.4m of occupied height in 828m of total structure (29.3% Vanity Ratio).

## When was Burj Khalifa built?

    The Burj Khalifa is 828 metres tall. This is the official architectural height recognised by the CTBUH and Guinness World Records. The absolute tip including a small communications needle reaches 829.8 metres.

### 2. How tall is the Burj Khalifa in feet?

The Burj Khalifa stands 2,717 feet tall to its architectural top. To the very tip it reaches 2,722 feet. The 2,717 ft figure is the one used in all official rankings.

### 3. How many floors does the Burj Khalifa have? [...] | Measurement | Value | Equivalent |

### Burj Khalifa Height in Metres – 828 m [...] You can check availability and secure your spot on our Burj Khalifa Tickets page.

## The Bottom Line on Burj Khalifa’s Height

The Burj Khalifa stands 828 metres (2,717 ft) tall, has 163 floors, and has been the world’s tallest building since 2009. Its spire adds 244 metres of architectural drama to a structure that would still be the tallest in the world even without it at 585 metres to the highest occupied floor. No other building comes close to matching it in 2026.

Summary: The Council on Tall Buildings and Urban Habitat recognizes Burj Khalifa in Dubai as the tallest building in the world at 828 m (2,717 ft) with 163 floors. This status was confirmed by the organization in 2010, and it remains the tallest building according to the sources provided. The Burj Khalifa surpassed the previous "World’s Tallest" building, Taipei 101, by 320 meters, an unprecedented increase of 61%. The building also holds records for "Height to Tip" and "Highest Occupied Floor".

Summary: The Council on Tall Buildings and Urban Habitat (CTBUH) has confirmed the "official building height" of the Burj Khalifa at 828 m (2,716.54 ft), confirming its title as "The World\'s Tallest Building". The building also contains a record-breaking number of floors, at 163. The architectural height of the Burj Khalifa is 828 m (2,717 ft), according to multiple sources including the CTBUH, Wikipedia, The Skyscraper Center, and Studio Matrx.

The building also contains a record-breaking number of floors, at 163; a record previously held by New York's World Trade Center (WTC) towers at 110 floors. [...] The Burj Khalifa has become the 16th building to hold the title of the "World's Tallest" and stands an additional 773 m, or 15 times taller, than the world's first "tall building" (the Home Insurance Building completed in Chicago in 1885).

sources.title: Burj Khalifa: How the Buttressed Core Made Height a Solved Problem — SOM's 828-metre tower in Dubai is not just the tallest building in the world — it is the moment structural height stopped being an engineering frontier and became a question of economics. This deep study reads its buttressed-core system, its wind-confusing setbacks, its record-breaking concrete, and the migrant labour the spire cannot rise above. | Studio Matrx

answer:
Burj Khalifa is taller than the Shanghai Tower, and the height difference is **196 metres**. [S4][S6]

- **Burj Khalifa (official height): 828 metres**. [S4]  
- **Shanghai Tower (official height): 632 metres**. [S6]  
- **Difference:** 828 − 632 = **196 metres**. [S4][S6]
